features.title: PostgreSQL socket ownership
features.why: P0c A ownership, B bounded wrapper lifecycle and C guard-negative qualification proved at the recorded head.

features.title: Design-negative sandbox closure
features.why: P0a widened the disposable fixture to match every path the decision trail cites; standalone design negatives are not yet wired into the pnpm check aggregate.

features.title: Toolchain and native readiness
features.why: P0b doctor implemented, review pending; mandatory CI, PostgreSQL hardening, React guards and hosted enforcement remain unimplemented.

features.title: Candidate pull request checks
features.why: Ordinary unprivileged GitHub test execution for pull requests to main. It is not trusted evidence, not merge authority, and the credential-bearing reporter remains a separate unqualified security task.

features.title: Mandatory local checks
features.why: A landing on local main needs a passing receipt for that exact commit; the hook is active only after install, and the Firstmate landing tool still has to call verify.

features.title: Owned project verification
features.why: Drive real isolated fixtures and retain proof without touching another attempt.

features.title: Trusted checks
features.why: Only the project's own reporting App, on the exact head and with a signed receipt, can satisfy a required check; live protection and App setup are blocked on human prerequisites.

features.title: Task proof admission
features.why: Reject missing or forged proof before a task can claim readiness.

features.title: Repository foundation
features.why: Prove real decisions and database isolation before product authority exists.

features.title: Portable wire contracts
features.why: Make the same bytes mean the same thing in TypeScript and Swift.

features.title: Client synchronization isolation
features.why: Keep replay, ordering and retry decisions independent of the renderer.

features.title: Local room
features.why: Owned local runtime, persistent messages and cursor replay, landed on main with L1, L2 and CI P0a-P0c, plus an independently testable L5 deterministic local-answer core and selected-message posting: browser or CLI triggers a committed, cited local-agent quote, not model inference. Browser retries persist an action command ID through lost response and clear it after receipt; cross-tab action races and full L5 qualification remain open. L4's first slice has landed: the apps/web room shell runs over a live Host transport, two tabs converge on committed history, a repeated Send keeps one identity and permanent rejections stop. Own sends no longer count as unread, the status announcement repeats the header's unread total, and phone buttons are 44 px. Remaining L4: real connection state with manual disconnect and read cancellation, per-command delivery states, session drafts, browser receipt-failure proof, measurements and a VoiceOver pass.

features.title: Living documentation and progress atlas
features.why: Make the system explain itself as each verified part lands.

features.title: Feature and Entrypoint discovery
features.why: U21.B01 discovers Features from each package's conventional src/features directory and generates a drift-checked inventory; live lanes, the perf probe and exact-head qualification are still open.

features.title: Application architecture boundaries
features.why: Make Feature/Client/Host and renderer shortcuts fail in lint and tests with owner-named diagnostics (B1 import ownership + B2a exact-row exception registry + B2b foot-guns).

features.title: Local room web shell
features.why: Give the browser one writer Client and typed EnvironmentPort, with the live room now styled to the approved light tokens and responsive shell while remaining in progress pending broader L4 qualification.

features.title: Timeline virtualization
features.why: Salvaged from a preserved source copy's Pretext/react-virtual implementation and integrated onto the current consolidated App.tsx behind the local apps/web/src/framework owner, so 50,000-message rooms mount only visible rows.

features.title: Message times
features.why: Show a locale-aware reading of the stored wire created_at, keep that value available for inspection, and leave committed-sequence order unchanged.

features.title: Agora application architecture
features.why: Give every product Feature an owned folder, discovered rather than registered, behind a one-writer Client and a typed Host. U20 boundary lint is Built and tracked separately as app-architecture, and U21.B01 discovery as feature-discovery. One U23.B01 construction slice moved the center's local-room adapter selection from apps/center/src/main.ts into its Feature Entrypoint; U23 is not qualified, the web renderer has not moved, and the U22 Client/Host boundary remains planned.

features.title: Encrypted backup and restore
features.why: The first U01c.B01 slice seals a disposable fixture database and its objects with AES-256-GCM, denies a wrong key, corruption, a missing file or a used target before writing, and restores into a second database whose row and object inventory must match. WAL, separate-host restore, off-host key recovery, epoch fencing and RPO/RTO remain open.

milestones.title: Establish repository contracts and test-first gates
milestones.outcome: An engineer can build a small contract fixture, observe a real red/green test, reject a forbidden import, and compile the same wire values in TypeScript and Swift.

milestones.title: Qualify isolated verification and trusted evidence
milestones.outcome: An engineer drives both real applications through their CLIs and cannot obtain a passing trusted result from forged or missing proof.

milestones.title: Prove independently recoverable backup and restore
milestones.outcome: An operator restores the foundation on a separate host, proves its data and fences the old instance.

milestones.title: Qualify the selected React production client
milestones.outcome: A user navigates a large room and failure/recovery cards in a responsive accessible client without authority confusion.

milestones.title: Establish application-architecture boundary lint
milestones.outcome: A renderer file that imports a storage or domain type, calls a browser global directly, or uses an unmediated effect fails lint with an error naming its supported owner.

milestones.title: Establish Feature and Entrypoint discovery
milestones.outcome: Adding a Feature with its reserved files makes it appear in the generated inventory automatically, and hand-editing that inventory instead of adding the reserved file fails the same way schema drift already fails.

milestones.title: Establish the Client and Host boundary
milestones.outcome: A component that holds durable timeline state in local state, or calls a browser global or transport directly, fails to build with an error naming the Client hook or Host method to use instead.

milestones.title: Migrate existing work into the Agora application architecture
milestones.outcome: The local-room feature's server entrypoint now lives in one discovered Feature folder, its generated inventory entry replaces the old hand-edited route registration, and every test that passed before the move still passes after it with an unchanged assertion.

milestones.title: Invite developers into scoped project rooms
milestones.outcome: Two invited humans sign in and see only rooms they may read; an owner can revoke a member and see active access end.

milestones.title: Deliver durable conversation and ordered reconnection
milestones.outcome: Two developers converse and search the same ordered history after reconnecting without duplicate messages or lost edits.

milestones.title: Answer questions with visible read-only agent sessions
milestones.outcome: A developer asks the center about a recorded decision and receives a cited answer without giving the agent execution or private-room authority.

milestones.title: Create owned tasks with fenced runs and approvals
milestones.outcome: A human confirms one bounded task; fake competing workers cannot both own it, and expired authority stays unusable.

milestones.title: Connect owner-bound workers and prepare clean worktrees
milestones.outcome: The launching developer connects a worker without inbound ports and receives an isolated task worktree while their normal checkout stays unchanged.

milestones.title: Execute bounded local work and collect behavior evidence
milestones.outcome: One real provider-backed task changes the fixture application, proves its user flow, and returns digest-verified evidence without host credential access.

milestones.title: Publish approved drafts and enforce independent review
milestones.outcome: The second developer approves an exact result, the owner publishes a draft, and GitHub blocks merge until independent review and trusted current-head checks pass.

milestones.title: Prove the first release across two accounts and machines
milestones.outcome: Two developers complete the entire conversation-to-local-task-to-human-reviewed-result workflow and an operator can restore the center.

milestones.title: Provision a private project from a conversation
milestones.outcome: An owner sees one repository and room with a truthful onboarding checkpoint; this milestone does not wait for future image/cloud units to activate the complete project.

milestones.title: Build and qualify declarative project images
milestones.outcome: A maintainer builds an approved project environment and can reproduce it after deleting its cache.

milestones.title: Execute and recover one isolated cloud attempt
milestones.outcome: A human launches a cloud task in a fresh microVM and sees evidence and confirmed destruction, or a precise unresolved cleanup state.

milestones.title: Activate persistent project agents and reviewed knowledge
milestones.outcome: A project main agent answers after restart with cited approved decisions, and stale/disputed knowledge no longer enters operational context.

milestones.title: Prove local and cloud execution parity
milestones.outcome: A developer chooses local or cloud explicitly and receives the same trustworthy review contract, while placement-specific trust and cost remain visible.

milestones.title: Enable conversational agent creation with isolated environments
milestones.outcome: A maintainer proposes an agent from a room and a second eligible human confirms its exact plan before any spend; self-confirmation and confirmation without the preview are both rejected.

milestones.title: Qualify a real external coding-agent adapter
milestones.outcome: A developer can use one qualified existing coding agent without granting it new authority.

milestones.title: Deliver the native Swift client without worker authority
milestones.outcome: Two developers use a real native Mac client for the same human-governed workflow without acquiring local execution authority.

milestones.title: Capture observer proposals and promote reviewed knowledge
milestones.outcome: A project conversation produces reviewable, attributed knowledge proposals without automatic truth or cross-project disclosure.

milestones.title: Harden operations and prove governed deletion
milestones.outcome: An operator can recover the center and explain every retained, deleted, or unresolved resource without hidden authority.

milestones.title: Add an opt-in notification-only Slack bridge
milestones.outcome: A requested Slack channel receives one approved notification linking to the authoritative Agora record, without becoming another control plane.

milestones.title: Deliver the built-in Bug Agent role
milestones.outcome: A Bug Agent reproduces a seeded defect, posts one cited finding, a repeat of the same defect updates that finding instead of duplicating it, and a human-approved repair task closes through the ordinary independent-review path.
